title: RBAC v2 -> Audit Pipeline + VPC Segmentation Hardening Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook maps RBAC v2 events through the audit/logging pipeline into SIEM ingestion, and ties those signals back to VPC segmentation patterns, firewall templates, and mTLS hardening required for Private deployments. The doc is intended for engineers implementing customer-specific Private installs and for security reviewers validating evidence automation.

Scope and goals:
- Define a minimal audit log schema for RBAC v2 that supports compliance audits (who, what, where, why, outcome).
- Provide example SIEM export mappings and recommended parsers (Elastic, Splunk, Sumo).
- Recommend VPC micro-segmentation patterns by deployment size (single-tenant, small multi-tenant, enterprise multi-az).
- Provide firewall rule templates and mTLS placement guidance (edge, service mesh, east-west).
- Checklist for evidence automation: artifact capture, retention, and verification scripts.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- RBAC events must include: actor_id, actor_type, role_changes, resource, action, result, api_path, request_id, timestamp, auth_chain (token id / cert thumbprint), client_ip, vpc_subnet, node_id.
- Export these fields to a compact JSON line format and ship to the forwarder using the field names below.
- Enforce network boundaries: control plane (management), inference plane (GPU nodes), admin subnet (SRE access), and customer-data zones. Use deny-by-default firewall rules and service-level allowlists.

Audit log schema (recommended fields and examples):
- timestamp: 2025-02-09T18:42:31Z
- request_id: rq_1a2b3c
- actor_id: user:priya@redwood.ai
- actor_type: human | service_account | external_key
- action: roles.update | auth.token.create | model.deploy | network.update
- resource: /v1/projects/prod/models/m-42
- role_changes: [{"role":"dedicated-admin","op":"add"}]
- result: success | failure:resource_not_found | failure:unauthorized
- auth_chain: ["token:tk_XX","cert:sha256:abcde..."]
- client_ip: 203.0.113.45
- vpc_subnet: 10.128.4.0/24
- node_id: gpu-cluster-22
- raw_payload_snippet: base64-encoded-first-512-bytes

SIEM export mapping (field -> destination key):
- timestamp -> @timestamp
- request_id -> event.id
- actor_id -> user.id
- actor_type -> user.type
- action -> event.action
- resource -> event.dataset_resource
- result -> event.outcome
- client_ip -> client.ip
- vpc_subnet -> network.subnet
- node_id -> host.name
- auth_chain -> event.authentication_chain

Example JSON line for forwarder:
{"@timestamp":"2025-02-09T18:42:31Z","event":{"id":"rq_1a2b3c","action":"roles.update","outcome":"success","dataset_resource":"/v1/projects/prod/models/m-42","authentication_chain":["token:tk_XX"]},"user":{"id":"user:priya@redwood.ai","type":"human"},"client":{"ip":"203.0.113.45"},"network":{"subnet":"10.128.4.0/24"},"host":{"name":"gpu-cluster-22"}}

Parsing notes for ops:
- Normalize actor_id prefixes (user:, svc:, ext:) with a transform during ingest to split identity_type and identity_value.
- Store role_changes as an indexed nested array in Elastic for fast queries.
- When result != success, include full raw_payload_snippet in long-term cold storage (S3) and index a pointer in the event.

VPC segmentation patterns (recommended):
- Single-tenant small: three subnets: mgmt (10.128.0.0/24), inference (10.128.1.0/24), storage (10.128.2.0/24). Default deny across subnets; explicit allow from mgmt->inference for orchestration ports (22/ssh, 8443/controlplane).
- Small multi-tenant: add per-tenant tenant-ns with /27 ranges inside inference zone and enforce host-based TLS + service-level identity.
- Enterprise multi-AZ: use AZ-local inference subnets, a central mgmt plane VPC peered with inference VPCs over encrypted tunnels, and egress IGW via controlled NAT gateways.

Firewall rule templates (deny-first):
- Global default: deny all ingress to inference subnets except mTLS-proxy and internal health checks.
- Allow mgmt->node: tcp/8443 (control), tcp/22 (bastion only from admin subnet), tcp/9090 (metrics, restricted).
- Allow node->storage: tcp/9000 (S3-compatible), tcp/2049 (NFS) from storage CIDR only.
- Allow service-mesh sidecar: ephemeral outbound high ports to other mesh peers, but restrict peer lists via service account identities.

mTLS placement and cert lifecycle (recommendation):
- Edge: TLS termination at the customer gateway; mTLS between gateway -> ingress-proxy (optional).
- East-West: mTLS enforced between all platform components in the inference plane. Use short-lived leaf certs minted by internal CA (Vault PKI).
- Rotation cadence: leaf certs 7 days, intermediate 90 days, CA rollover planning window 180 days. Automate rotation with a preflight test that validates chain and audits via RBAC event logging.

Evidence automation checklist (implementation steps):
1) On every RBAC change event, create an immutable record in the audit index and emit a signed evidence artifact (signed_manifest) containing the event JSON, base64 payload snippet, and a hash (sha256).
2) Forward the event to the SIEM forwarder (TLS + mutual auth). Include request_id and signed_manifest_id in headers for traceability.
3) Store signed artifacts in WORM storage bucket with lifecycle: hot (30d), cold (365d), archive (7y) depending on customer compliance profile.
4) Daily verification job: sample 1% of artifacts, validate signature and hash, run replay against a sandbox SIEM parser and flag mismatches to a ticket in JIRA-SEC-AUDIT.
5) On any discrepancy, auto-create evidence bundle (signed) and notify the customer admin and security contacts per the contract SLA.

Operational playbook snippets (incident focused):
- Unauthorized role assignment detected (result: failure:unauthorized) -> auto-block: run revoke for session tokens tied to actor_id, escalate to on-call via PagerDuty, create incident with attachment: evidence bundle (signed_manifest, raw_snippet pointer).
- Suspicious lateral movement: alert on repeated cross-subnet node-to-node API calls from same client_ip; trigger firewall temporary deny for that ip and capture PCAP for 72 hours to S3.

Diagram (ASCII, rough):
[Admin Subnet]--(SSH/Bastion)->[Mgmt Plane]--(mTLS)->[Ingress Proxy]--(mTLS)->[Service Mesh]->[GPU Nodes]
          |                                                        |
   (metrics)                                                   (storage)

Operational TODOs (short term):
- PR: add event.authentication_chain to rbac proto (github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-proto/pull/78) - Diego
- SIEM: build ingest parser for Elastic and validate with sample logs (JIRA-SEC-4312) - Priya
- Infra: create TF module for default deny firewall and preflight test harness - Samir

Open questions / risk notes:
- How do we handle non-TLS metadata from legacy connectors? (do not allow on production installs; add translation gateway for legacy connectors in lab.)
- Cross-tenant telemetry correlation for multi-tenant small installs may leak tenant IDs unless request_id is namespaced. Enforce namespacing at auth token issuance.

Appendix: sample revoke command (ops):
- /bin/redwoodctl sessions revoke --actor user:alice@cust.com --since 2025-02-09T00:00:00Z --reason "suspicious role update"

References:
- Confluence: RBAC v2 spec (linked above)
- Vault PKI automation doc (internal)
- SIEM ingestion template examples (Elastic: ingest-pipeline.json)

Notes to reviewers: this is a working draft for the private-deploy install checklist. Feed back with concrete parser field names or additional evidence retention windows.
